sections.html:
Anderson is the county seat of Anderson County, in the northwest corner of South Carolina on the Piedmont plateau. It sits roughly at the midpoint of the Interstate 85 corridor, about 120 miles from Atlanta and 140 miles from Charlotte, and about an hour from the Blue Ridge Mountains.

The city is compact. It covers 15.86 square miles at an elevation of 738 feet. The 2020 census counted 28,106 people in 11,282 households, which made it the 16th most populous city in the state. The Census Bureau's 2025 estimate is 31,323, and the median age is 36.6.

Those numbers describe the city limits only. The county around Anderson is much larger, and rules for a house just outside the limits can differ from those inside.

sections.h2: Why is Anderson called the Electric City?
sections.html:
William C. Whitner started electric service in 1895 from a hydroelectric plant on the Rocky River, and the city became one of the first in the Southeast with power. It was also the first in the world to run a cotton gin on electricity.

The Portman Dam washed away in 1901, which left the city dark until it was rebuilt in 1902. The area was first settled in 1826 and the city takes its name from Robert Anderson, a Revolutionary War veteran who explored the region. Johnson Female Seminary opened in 1848, and a Confederate monument from 1902 stands facing the county courthouse.

Anderson's name for itself rests on that early power story, and the city still treats it as part of its identity. Anyone selling an older house here is selling into a place with deep industrial roots, and a buyer will expect the age of the wiring, plumbing and roof to be disclosed.

sections.h2: What does Anderson's economy look like?
sections.html:
Manufacturing leads. Anderson has more than 230 manufacturers, 22 of them international, making automotive products, plastics, metal products, industrial machinery, publishing materials and textiles.

  • Glen Raven runs its largest manufacturing center here, producing Sunbrella fabrics.
  • AnMed is the primary health network and one of the county's top employers, centered on AnMed Medical Center.
  • More than 27 BMW suppliers operate across the Upstate.
  • Anderson University, a private school with about 3,900 students, and Tri-County Technical College add education employers, along with Carolina Bible College.

Because so many local jobs are in factories and a single hospital network, owners who need to relocate for work may not want to wait through a long listing period.

sections.h2: How do roads, schools and weather shape life in Anderson?
sections.html:
Interstate 85 is the city's only freeway, with five signed exits. US 29, US 76, US 178 and SC 187 also pass through. Anderson Regional Airport is about 3 miles away, and the nearest commercial airport is Greenville-Spartanburg International, about 42 miles. Six local bus routes run roughly hourly.

The city is served by Anderson School District Five, with 11 elementary schools, 5 middle schools and 2 high schools, Westside High and T. L. Hanna High.

The climate is humid subtropical. July highs average about 91 degrees and January highs about 53. Yearly precipitation is about 50 inches, and snow averages under an inch. With that much rain, roofs, gutters and moisture under the house are worth checking before a buyer's inspector does.

sections.h2: What does Anderson's code enforcement do about neglected houses?
sections.html:
The City of Anderson enforces nuisance rules for excessive weeds and grass, debris in yards, substandard and dilapidated housing, and abandoned vehicles. To report a violation, call (864) 231-2217 or use the Request Service button on the city website.

The process runs in stages and takes about 4 to 6 weeks, according to the city.

  1. A courtesy summons goes to the owner, tenant or person in charge. The case closes if the problem is fixed in 14 days.
  2. If it is not, the Building Department issues a Uniform Ordinance Summons and a hearing is scheduled at least 10 days after service.
  3. For owners who cannot be found or live outside the city, certified mail is used and hearings are set at least 30 days out.

If a summons cannot be served in person, it is posted on the property and mailed to the owner listed on the tax records. That is one reason to keep your mailing address current with the county. A seller who lives elsewhere can miss a notice for weeks.

sections.h2: What permits and fees can slow a repair before you sell?
sections.html:
Anderson requires permits for new construction, repairs and renovations, including building, electrical, plumbing, mechanical, demolition and sign permits. Applications go through the city's online ViewPoint Cloud system, and contractors need a state license plus a city business license.

The city's fee schedule, effective July 1, 2022, shows two details sellers should know. Starting work before getting a permit brings a $200 fine and doubles the permit fee. Re-inspections cost $50 each. The page lists the department at the Municipal Business Center, 601 S. Main St., but its footer shows a different street number, so confirm the address before you visit.

Fixing a house to list it conventionally means permits, inspections and contractor time. A cash sale as-is avoids those steps for the seller.

sections.h2: What does selling an Anderson house require under state law?
sections.html:
Most sellers of one to four unit homes must give the buyer a written property condition disclosure statement. State law lets the parties agree in writing not to complete it, and it allows as-is sales. A seller who knowingly gives false or incomplete information can be liable for damages and costs.

A South Carolina attorney must supervise the closing, because the State Bar treats drafting, closing and recording as the practice of law. The deed is recorded at the Anderson County Register of Deeds, 401 East River Street, open Monday through Friday from 8:30 a.m. to 5:00 p.m. Documents must be submitted by 4:30 p.m.

The state deed recording fee is $1.85 per $500 of the price, with the county keeping $0.55. The register offers free fraud alerts, and property records are on the county's ACPASS site.

sections.h2: How is property tax handled when an Anderson house is sold?
sections.html:
Under state law, tax is payable from September 30 through January 15, with penalties of 3 percent on January 16, another 7 percent after the second day of February and another 5 percent after March 17. A sale is a reappraisal event, and an owner-occupied home is assessed at 4 percent only if the owner applied.

Any unpaid tax is settled from the sale proceeds at closing, and the closing attorney handles the payoff. Anderson County has its own tax guide on this site with office details.

faqs.q: Why is Anderson, SC nicknamed the Electric City?
faqs.a: Because it had electric service in 1895 from a hydroelectric plant on the Rocky River, early for the Southeast. It was also the first in the world to power a cotton gin with electricity.

faqs.q: How many people live in Anderson, SC?
faqs.a: The 2020 census counted 28,106 residents, and the Census Bureau's 2025 estimate is 31,323.

faqs.q: What happens if the city cites my Anderson house for overgrown grass or debris?
faqs.a: You first get a courtesy summons with 14 days to fix it. If the problem remains, a Uniform Ordinance Summons follows and a court hearing is set. The city says the process takes about 4 to 6 weeks.

faqs.q: Can I sell my Anderson house as-is?
faqs.a: Yes. South Carolina law allows as-is agreements. You still need to give a disclosure statement unless both sides agree in writing not to, and the closing must be supervised by an attorney.

faqs.q: Where do I find Anderson County property records?
faqs.a: The Register of Deeds is at 401 East River Street, phone (864) 260-4054, and property records are online through ACPASS.
